tagline: Gravel between two highways, with the Alaska Range above.
intro: Out of Paxson, the Denali Highway climbs into the foothills of the Alaska Range, with pavement as far as Tangle Lakes and gravel for most of the way beyond. The first 45 miles wind through the Amphitheater Mountains to Maclaren Summit. Then the road drops into the Maclaren River valley, crosses the Susitna, and follows the Nenana down to Cantwell.

It was commissioned on August 5, 1957, as the first road access to Denali National Park. A private car had driven the length of it three days earlier. The Parks Highway later took over that duty, and the old approach remains a 135-mile crossing, with glaciers in view when the weather allows.

moments.title: Tangle Lakes
moments.text: Streams join this chain of lakes into the headwaters of the Delta River, with a boat launch at Round Tangle Lake beside the highway.

moments.title: Maclaren Summit
moments.text: The highway crests at 4,086 feet, and a BLM trail at milepost 39 leads north into alpine terrain that birders seek out.

moments.title: Cantwell
moments.text: The western end of the highway meets a settlement that began as an Alaska Railroad flag stop supplying the Valdez Creek mines.

practical: Most of the highway is gravel, with washboarding and dust; winter travel is by snowmobile or dogsled.
